function: DRL (PPO) selects DFT-codebook beams per user each TTI for a monostatic OFDM ISAC base station, jointly minimizing latency and range/velocity estimation error (pp. 7-8).
system: Monostatic full-duplex OFDM ISAC BS, N_T=16 ULA Tx plus N_R ULA Rx, two single-antenna users, 28 GHz, 60 kHz spacing; no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: Reinforcement learning: PPO agent with fully connected policy (two hidden layers of 128 nodes), trained offline in simulation; DQN, A2C, TD7 also trained for comparison (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS channel without clutter, Rician (K=10) with four stationary clutters; two vehicles in a 100 m x 100 m area; no standard model or dataset (p. 9).
test_conditions: Test: 500 episodes, initial positions from a set disjoint from training; mean speed 6-14 m/s; with and without clutter. No other-scenario test reported (p. 9).
baselines: Non-learned: X-TDMA beam sweeping, AoD-based MUSIC heuristic, Genie bound, Xie [15] optimization with CSI. Learned: DQN, A2C, TD7, PPO-1b single-beam variant (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Throughput CDF, average latency, latency distribution, probability that normalized range, velocity or angle error is below 0.2, average training reward (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Order of runtime complexity per TTI, O(sum of n_{l-1} n_l) over fully connected layers; network has two hidden layers of 128 nodes (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 9: "the channel between the BS and a user is assumed to have Rician fading with a Rician K-factor of 10". Custom simulator with Rician fading and clutters; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data (3GPP appears only as the beam alignment protocol of the X-TDMA baseline).
q2_support: p. 9: "user positions initialized randomly from a test set that is disjoint from the training set". Only a held-out set of initial positions of the same scenario; no new scenario, band, antenna or user count is tested and no adaptation is reported.
q3_support: p. 9: "PPO surpasses A2C after more than 12k training episodes"; p. 10: "The PPO-based method outperforms the AoD-based and X-TDMA methods". DQN, A2C and TD7 are compared only on the training reward (Fig. 3), which is latency plus sensing performance (p. 8).
q4_support: p. 11: "total runtime complexity of" one TTI is O(sum of n_{l-1} n_l); "the implemented neural network has 2 hidden layers, each with 128 nodes".
q5_support: p. 8: "The simulation parameters are summarized in Table I". Own simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset (the only URL is a Hexa-X-II report in the references, p. 13).
notes: Preprint (arXiv 2604.24369v1). Cross-layer: buffer state is an input, but the learned decision is the beam allocation (physical layer), so above_phy does not apply; power allocation is not learned (p. 7). q3 is borderline: the learned baselines DQN, A2C and TD7 are compared with PPO only on the average training reward (Fig. 3, p. 9), not on test throughput, latency or error, and PPO-1b is the authors' own variant and does not count; non-learned X-TDMA, AoD-based, Xie [15] and Genie are compared on throughput, latency and errors (pp. 9-11). Reviewer to confirm q3.
